# Closure and Escalation Notes

**Deception - Honey Credentials File Opened** · `T1552.001_honey_file_access` · [T1552.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/)

Fill in only what you checked. A confirmed attack is never closed from the queue: send the escalation note instead.

## Benign Positive

The rule fired on real activity that is expected and authorized.

```text
Alert:        T1552.001_honey_file_access for <host> at <time, UTC>
Observed:     EventID=<value>  ObjectType=<value>  ObjectName=<value>  AccessList=<value>
Checked:      1. Confirm the file is a decoy in deceive/decoys.yml and that no data-classification scan or migration was declared for the time -> <result>
              2. Identify the accessing account (SubjectUserName) and, for a share access, the client host from the matching 5145 event on the server -> <result>
              3. Check whether the credentials inside the file were tried afterwards - the honey account rule fires on every attempt -> <result>
Benign:       <which known source below> - confirmed by <change record, owner or ticket>
Disposition:  Benign Positive
Tuning:       none | machine_account (applied) | search_indexer (applied) | classification_agent_account (proposed)
```

Known benign sources for this detection:
- A data-classification or backup agent that runs under a user account instead of the machine account
- A curious employee who opens a file named passwords

Never tune:
- Never filter by client host or by business hours: the decoys exist to catch any account from anywhere.
- Never widen the filters to a process name an attacker can choose, such as explorer.exe or powershell.exe.
- Never drop a decoy from the rule without removing it from deceive/decoys.yml; rasd deceive --check fails on the difference.

```text
              The share access events (5140, 5145) of the same session on the server, with the client address -> <where it is saved>
              Logons of the account on the client host and the server around the access -> <where it is saved>
              The decoy's history in the inventory (when it was planted, by whom) -> <where it is saved>
Containment:  none yet | <action taken, time UTC>

```

Escalate when any of these holds:
1. The account is not a documented administrator of the share
2. The decoy credentials were used afterwards (a honey account alert from the same hour)
3. Several decoy files, or decoys on several servers, were opened by the same account

Risk conditions: outside business hours +10 · host is critical +5 · approved admin activity -40.

Containment options, after the evidence above is preserved:
1. Disable or reset the accessing account
2. Isolate the client host
3. Rotate any real credential the account could have reached; keep the decoy and record the touch in the deception log
